findings.title: Sensitive operation answers anonymous callers
findings.description: Requests with no credential at all got a 2xx response from an endpoint that returns sensitive data or changes state.
findings.detail: GET /api/v1/products/{product_id} (productpage) returned 2xx to 30 request(s) without a token
findings.recommendation: Add authentication to GET /api/v1/products/{product_id} in productpage.
mitigation: Require a verified token on this operation in the service itself, not only at the gateway.
Reject requests without Authorization with 401 before any business logic runs.
Add a test that calls the endpoint anonymously and expects 401.

findings.title: Public entry serves the API without TLS
findings.description: The public entry (Ingress, load balancer, Istio Gateway or published port) has no TLS, so Authorization headers and personal data sent through it can be read or replayed on the network. The evidence says how many public endpoints carried them in this capture.
findings.detail: Istio Gateway bookinfo-gateway serves the API over plain HTTP
findings.recommendation: Enable TLS on Istio Gateway bookinfo-gateway.
mitigation: Terminate TLS at the ingress (tls: section + certificate) and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
Send Strict-Transport-Security so browsers never fall back to HTTP.

findings.title: Calls from an unidentified internal caller
findings.description: Traces start at this backend endpoint, so the caller is not instrumented and did not come through the gateway. Monitoring cannot say who made these calls.
findings.detail: 4 trace(s) start at ratings POST /ratings/{productId} with no traced caller
evidence: no parent span from the gateway or another service
findings.recommendation: Identify and instrument the caller of POST /ratings/{productId}.
mitigation: Instrument every job and client that calls internal APIs (propagate traceparent).
Require caller identity on internal endpoints so logs name the caller.

findings.title: Service-to-service call accepted without credentials
findings.description: Another microservice calls this endpoint without any credential and it succeeds, so any pod that can reach it can do the same (no zero-trust between services).
findings.detail: productpage -> GET /details/{id} (details) with no credential
factors: likelihood -1: reachable only inside the cluster
evidence: no mTLS enforced for details (no STRICT PeerAuthentication or mesh injection)
findings.recommendation: Require service identity (mTLS or a service token) on /details/{id} in details.
mitigation: Authenticate workloads to each other: mTLS through a service mesh, or signed service tokens.
Authorize per caller: only order-service may call /charge, for example.
findings.snippet:
# Istio: require mTLS and allow only order-service
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
spec:
  rules:
  - from:
    - source: {principals: ["cluster.local/ns/shoplite/sa/order-service"]}
